understanding.purpose: Audit English-language dependencies for their versions, licenses, vulnerabilities, and relevant notes.
understanding.reading: Readers scan package names to find a dependency, then read across its row; they may also compare licenses and vulnerabilities down their columns.
groups: Package and Version identify the dependency and the release being audited.
License and Vulnerabilities are compact audit fields that readers may compare across packages.
Notes provide explanatory context for the same row and may need more reading space.
keep_intact: License identifiers and vulnerability values where possible
may_wrap: Long package names at natural separator boundaries where possible

preferred.name: r2A
preferred.note: Keep r1A's readable identifying and audit columns, and give Notes its full 252px longest-word width. This tests whether eliminating the remaining forced split and reducing row height justify the extra scrolling.

acceptable.name: r1A
acceptable.note: Keep the intact identifier and audit columns from r0C, but reduce Notes to trade some note wrapping for 63px less horizontal scrolling.

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: Widen Notes moderately from r1A to improve wrapping while limiting added horizontal travel. Retain the package and version widths that preserve their readable breaks.

acceptable.name: r3A
acceptable.note: Keep r2A’s intact versions, audit fields, and notes, while giving the long package identifier 12px more room to improve its wrapping.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: Test a more generous Package column to see whether the scoped identifier becomes easier to read as a unit, accepting additional horizontal scrolling.

bad.name: r1B
bad.note: Narrow Package and Version enough to bring more of License into the initial viewport, while retaining a substantial Notes column. Check whether the scoped package and prerelease version wrap acceptably.
bad.why: The narrow package and version columns split identifiers within words, making the long package name and prerelease version harder to read.

bad.name: r1C
bad.note: Preserve the core audit fields from r0C and use a narrower Notes column to reduce scrolling further. This tests whether the resulting row heights remain manageable.
bad.why: The narrow notes column drives several rows to four or five lines, creating a tall table and making it harder to scan across rows.

bad.name: r2C
bad.note: Reduce Version slightly and give Notes a little more room than r1A. This tests a compromise that brings the audit columns closer to the initial viewport while checking whether the beta version remains readable.
bad.why: The version column splits the prerelease identifier, while the narrower notes column makes several rows taller.

rationale: r2A keeps identifiers and notes free of mid-word splits while limiting cells to three lines, so rows remain easier to scan. Its first viewport shows the package and version columns and most of the license column; vulnerabilities and notes require horizontal scrolling. Wider package columns in r3A and r3B do not improve row heights and push more of the license column beyond the initial view.

general: Preserve identifiers and version strings where possible; mid-word breaks make them harder to recognize and compare.
Allocate width to columns that reduce disruptive wrapping, while considering what readers can see before scrolling.
specific: The long notes content needs substantially more width than the other columns to avoid splits and excessive row height.
The long package name wraps at r2A's width, but its breaks do not force additional row height beyond that already needed by the notes.

tradeoffs: r2A requires 416px of horizontal scrolling to reach the table's far edge. A designer who values a shorter horizontal journey more than intact words and compact rows could prefer r1A or r2B.
uncertain: The ranges are approximate judgments around r2A, not browser-verified thresholds. The best balance also depends on how often readers need vulnerabilities and notes alongside package names.

critique.good: All five columns are available at first sight, and the package column gives readers a starting point for each row.
critique.problems: The table is extremely tall and difficult to scan. Headers and identifiers fragment, notes become narrow vertical streams, and large row heights make comparison between packages laborious.
critique.cause: The 49px Version, 55px License, 75px Vulnerabilities, and 75px Notes columns leave too little content width. Even the 105px Package column splits the long scoped identifier.

critique.good: The first viewport shows package names, versions, and licenses, with a glimpse of the vulnerability column. Headers stay intact, and the long package name wraps at useful separators.
critique.problems: The prerelease version wraps, and the narrow Notes column produces tall rows that weaken the connection between neighboring records. Vulnerabilities and notes require horizontal scrolling.
critique.cause: The 75px Version column leaves 54px for content, while the 150px Notes column leaves 129px. The table is 256px wider than the viewport.

critique.good: Versions and license identifiers remain intact, package names wrap at separators, and the wider notes produce compact, readable rows without mid-word splits.
critique.problems: The first viewport ends within the License column, leaving the entire Vulnerabilities and Notes columns offscreen. The long horizontal journey makes reading across a row less convenient.
critique.cause: The 112px Version, 98px License, 124px Vulnerabilities, and 273px Notes columns preserve content well but bring the total width to 775px, excluding the table's outer border.

critique.good: Package and Version read clearly together, the long package wraps at separators, and the headers stay on one line. The wider Notes column gives rows a more manageable height than r1C.
critique.problems: The first viewport reaches only through License, so the vulnerability findings and notes require horizontal scrolling. One mid-word split remains, and the long package row is considerably taller than the short rows.
critique.cause: The first three columns total 378px, while the 210px Notes column leaves 189px for text, less than its 252px longest unbreakable item. The 713px table requires substantial sideways travel.

critique.good: The narrower identifying columns bring the beginning of Vulnerabilities into the first viewport and reduce the total scrolling distance.
critique.problems: The long scoped package breaks inside a word, and its beta version breaks across lines. These splits make the identifier and release harder to read together; the saved width also comes with a taller row.
critique.cause: Package provides 129px of text space, below its 147px longest unbreakable word, and Version provides 74px, below its 91px one-line content width. Notes is also 10px narrower than in r1A.

critique.good: Package and Version retain the clearer treatment of r1A, and all headers remain intact. The table is narrower than r1A.
critique.problems: The narrower Notes column makes several rows conspicuously tall and leaves large areas of empty space in the shorter audit fields. The first viewport still ends before Vulnerabilities.
critique.cause: Notes provides only 144px of text space, producing up to five lines in a cell and increasing the table height to 498px. The first three columns still total 378px.

critique.good: The strongest overall balance: headers remain intact, versions and license identifiers are readable, and the long package name wraps at separators. Notes fit without mid-word splits, keeping rows to three lines or fewer.
critique.problems: The first viewport shows the identifying fields and most of License, but reaching Vulnerabilities and Notes requires substantial horizontal scrolling. The long package name still occupies three lines.
critique.cause: The 168px Package column leaves 147px for text, while the 273px Notes column is needed to accommodate its 252px unbreakable string. Together with the intact audit fields, these widths produce a 776px table.

critique.good: Package, Version, License, and the headers retain the same readable treatment as r2A, with slightly less horizontal scrolling.
critique.problems: A note splits mid-word and grows to four lines, making its row taller and weakening the row’s visual rhythm. The 33px saving does little to change what is visible initially.
critique.cause: Reducing Notes from 273px to 240px leaves only 219px for text, less than its 252px longest unbreakable string.

critique.good: This is the narrowest table, and all headers remain on one line. The package name continues to wrap at separators.
critique.problems: The beta version wraps, making the identifying fields harder to scan together. A note still splits mid-word, and several rows become taller, creating more empty space in their shorter cells.
critique.cause: The 105px Version column leaves 84px for text, less than its 91px one-line requirement. The 220px Notes column leaves only 199px, forcing a split in its longest unbreakable string.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r2B.why: Package names and versions are mostly readable, and the long package wraps at recognizable breaks. The first viewport shows only the first three columns, so the audit findings require horizontal scrolling.

ref_equal.why: All columns fit in the viewport, but headers, package names, license names and notes break into fragments. The resulting tall rows make comparisons difficult.

ref_auto.why: The package column is readable and the long name wraps reasonably, but the prerelease version splits and vulnerabilities are only just visible at the viewport edge.

r1B.why: The long package name breaks within words, the prerelease version splits, and tall rows add space without making the audit columns visible.

r1A.why: Versions stay intact and the long package name wraps at recognizable breaks. Tall rows and the need to scroll past the first three columns make scanning less efficient.

r2A.why: The visible columns balance readable package names, intact versions and a compact row rhythm. Vulnerabilities and notes still require horizontal scrolling.

raw.unsure: The supplied views do not show the full right-hand portion of the scrolling layouts, so the widths and wrapping of vulnerabilities and notes cannot be fully assessed.

r1A.why: Package names and versions are mostly readable, but the tall rows leave considerable empty space, and vulnerabilities and notes lie beyond the initial viewport.

r2A.why: The first three columns are easy to scan, the long package name wraps at useful breaks, and the rows remain relatively compact. Vulnerabilities and notes require horizontal scrolling.

ref_equal.why: All five columns fit, but headers, package identifiers and notes split into fragments. The resulting tall rows make comparisons difficult.

ref_auto.why: Package names and licenses read reasonably well, but the prerelease version splits across lines and only a sliver of vulnerabilities appears initially.

r1B.why: The long package name breaks within a word, the prerelease version wraps, and tall rows contain substantial empty space. Most audit details require scrolling.

r2B.why: Versions remain intact and the long package name wraps at useful breaks, but the tall rows are sparse and vulnerabilities and notes are outside the initial viewport.

raw.unsure: The supplied views show only the left portion of the wider layouts, so I cannot assess the widths and wrapping of their off-screen vulnerabilities and notes columns.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
